source_text:
Μὴ μόνον οὖν αὐτὸν καλῶμεν κύριον: οὐ γὰρ τοῦτο σώσει ἡμᾶς.
λέγει γάρ: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι: Κύριε, κύριε, σωθήσεται, ἀλλ’ ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην.
ὥστε οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτὸν ὁμολογῶμεν, ἐν τῷ ἀγαπᾶν ἑαυτούς, ἐν τῷ μὴ μοιχᾶσθαι μηδὲ καταλαλεῖν ἀλλήλων μηδὲ ζηλοῦν, ἀλλ’ ἐγκρατεῖς εἶναι, ἐλεήμονας, ἀγαθούς: καὶ συμπάσχειν ἀλλήλοις ὀφείλομεν, καὶ μὴ φιλαργυρεῖν. ἐν τούτοις τοῖς ἔργοις ὁμολογῶμεν αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἐναντίοις:
καὶ οὐ δεῖ ἡμᾶς φοβεῖσθαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μᾶλλον, ἀλλὰ τὸν θεόν.
διὰ τοῦτο, ταῦτα ὑμῶν πρασσόντων, εἶπεν ὁ κύριος: Ἐὰν ἦτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ συνηγμένοι ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ μου καὶ μὴ ποιῆτε τὰς ἐντολάς μου, ἀποβαλῶ ὑμᾶς καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν: Ὑπάγετε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς, πόθεν ἐστέ, ἐργάται ἀνομίας.
orientation: The preacher has just quoted Isaiah on lip-service and now urges the congregation to confess Christ through actions, not by calling him Lord alone.
pass_a_gloss: Not only therefore him let us call Lord: not for this will save us. For he says: Not every [one] saying to me: Lord, Lord, will be saved, but the [one] doing the righteousness. So therefore, brothers, in the works him let us confess, in the loving one another, in the not committing adultery nor speaking evil of one another nor being jealous, but self-controlled to be, merciful, good: and to suffer with one another we owe, and not to love money. In these the works let us confess him and not in the opposite [ones]: and not it is necessary [for] us to fear the men more, but the God. Through this, these [things] of you doing, said the Lord: If you are with me gathered close in the bosom of me and not you do the commandments of me, I will cast away you and I will say to you: Go away from me, not I know you, from where you are, workers of lawlessness.

choices.why: Glossary term; the article makes it the specific righteousness God requires.
Glossary term for ἐγκράτεια; here the adjective form.
Compound verb; the συν- prefix means sharing in one another's suffering.
Compound of φιλέω and ἄργυρος; literal sense of loving silver/money.
κόλπος means bosom or lap; the image is of intimate gathering with Christ.
ἀνομία is lawlessness, not just sin; the phrase echoes Matthew 7:23.

pass_b_english: So let us not merely call him Lord, for that will not save us.
He himself says, "Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will be saved, but only the one who does righteousness."

Therefore, brothers, let us confess him in our deeds: by loving one another, by not committing adultery, by not speaking evil of one another, by not being jealous, but by being self-controlled, merciful, and good. We ought also to suffer with one another and not love money. It is by these deeds that we confess him, and not by their opposites.
And we must not fear human beings more than we fear God.

For this reason, when you do these things, the Lord said: "If you are gathered close to me in my bosom and do not keep my commandments, I will cast you away and say to you, 'Go away from me; I do not know where you come from, you workers of lawlessness.'"

last_rejected.why: Brief bans 'money'; glossary maps mammon/φιλαργυρεῖν to 'mammon'.
last_rejected.ruling: φιλαργυρεῖν means 'love money/avarice'; 'mammon' is a transliteration, not required translation.

last_rejected.why: Source 'γάρ' introduces Scripture with no 'himself'; adds emphasis not in Greek.
last_rejected.ruling: λέγει γάρ means 'for he says'; 'himself' adds mild emphasis but doesn't change meaning or mislead the reader.

The source introduces the saying with 'εἶπεν ὁ κύριος' (the Lord said), and the English faithfully renders this. The source itself does not identify whether it is a canonical quote, a non-canonical saying, or a paraphrase, so no clarification is warranted.
